newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: ANZ's NZ staff vow to fight on for wage rise.
newsitem.headline: ANZ's NZ staff vow to fight on for wage rise.

text.p: ANZ Bank's New Zealand staff on Monday rejected the bank's offer of a 3.5 percent wage increase and vowed to embark on a campaign of industrial action to see their wage demands met, a union spokesman said.
"They're very angry. They feel that they've been trampled on for a number of years," said Paul Goulter, general secretary of the Finance Sector Union (Finsec).
"They voted overwhelmingly to engage in a campaign of industrial action which will be called at short notice and obviously only will be disclosed at very short notice."
Goulter said ANZ staff had yet to decide whether to call a national strike or take targeted industrial action.
He said staff around the country voted to reject the bank's offer of a 3.5 percent wage rise because only a six percent increase would bring ANZ wage rates into line with other banks.
ANZ said in a statement it had not been informed of any further action.

The bank reiterated its claim that the offered wage rise would yield a total increase for ANZ staff of 7.25 percent over two years, which surpassed cost-of-living increases and shares gains made in productivity.
But Goulter slammed ANZ's rationale as a "joke".
"That's a joke of an argument. Why didn't they go back four years? Why didn't they go back 24 years?," he asked.
"It's absolutely ridiculous, and if you do that comparison with other banks of course it shows them even further out of kilter. Quite frankly I think that's an insult to staff."
Goulter said there were about 4,500 ANZ staff covered by the contract in question.
